items.title: 마벨, 루멘텀 154조에 인수

items.title: 국내 증시 흔드는 AI 투자 불안…"빅테크 투자금 회수 우려 과도"
items.snippet: 미국 빅테크의 인공지능(AI) 투자 수익성에 대한 불안이 국내 증시에도 부담으로 작용하는 가운데, 투자금 회수 실패 가능성에 대한 시장의 우려가 과도하다는 분석이 나왔다.최근 빅테크의 대규모 설비투자로 잉여현금흐름(FCF)은 악화하고 있지만, AI 인프라 수요가 견조하고 이를 활용한 클라우드 사업의 매출과 이익도 늘고 있어 투자금 회수 가능성은 여전히 높다는 진단이다.강재구 하나증권 연구원은 2일 보고서에서 "견조한 수요와 실제 사업 성과를 고려하면 현재의 현금흐름 악화를 AI 투자의 수익성 저하로 해석하기는 어렵다"고 밝혔다.우

items.title: 젠슨 황도 '물린' 네이버, 엔비디아 협력으로 반등 모멘텀 얻나

items.title: 씨엠티엑스, 3분기 영업익 105억…전년비 32% 급감

items.title: 껑충 뛴 탄소배출권 가격…타이트한 수급에 고공행진 불가피

items.snippet: “‘원팀 코리아’의 글로벌 허브가 되겠다.” 흩어져 있는 공공기관 해외 사무소를 한곳에 모아 ‘원스톱’ 행정 서비스를 제공하는 ‘케이(K)-마루’가 2일 중국 베이징에서 문을 열었다. 정부는 베이징을 비롯해 미국 로스앤젤레스, 베트남 하노이 등 세계 7개 거점에서 K-마루를 운영할 예정이다. 이곳에선 기업 지원, 민원 상담 등을 통합 제공한다. 이날 베이징 차오양구 왕징 포스코센터에선 ‘베이징 K-마루’ 현판식이 열렸다. K-마루는 한국을 뜻하는 ‘K’와 한옥의 바닥 공간인 ‘마루’를 합친 용어다. 베이징 K-마루는 포스코센터 11, 12층을 리모델링한 전용 공간으로, 공공기관 사무실 외에도 스마트 회의실과 민원 접견실이 마련됐다. 현재 8개 공공기관이 입주를 마쳤고, 2031년까지 총 22곳이 입주할 예정이다. 전 세계에서 조성 중인 K-마...

items.title: 北, 한미 연합연습에 “더 강력한 핵으로 통제”
items.snippet: 최근 한미 군 당국이 북핵 위협에 대응하는 핵·재래식 통합(CNI) 도상연습(TTX) ‘아이언 메이스(Iron Mace·철퇴)’를 실시한 것을 두고 북한이 “극악한 핵전쟁 시연”이라며 강하게 반발했다. ‘강철비’로 불리는 집속탄 발사 시험을 주도한 미사일 개발의 핵심 책임자가 이례적으로 담화에 나서면서 한미 연합훈련을 명분으로 북한이 고강도 도발에 나설 수 있다는 우려가 나온다. 김정식 노동당 중앙위원회 군수공업부 제1부부장은 2일 조선중앙통신에 발표한 담화에서 최근 한미 군 당국의 아이언 메이스 연습을 언급하며 “철두철미 우리 국가에 대한 핵무기 사용을 목적으로 한 가장 극악한 핵전쟁 시연”이라고 주장했다. 그는 “2024년부터 연례적으로 강행되고 있는 아이언 메이스는 우리를 핵으로 압살하려는 미국의 야망은 변함이 없으며 그 위험 수위가 날...

items.title: 공군, 美우주군 주관 ‘국제 워게임’ 첫 참가
items.snippet: 한국 공군이 미 우주군이 주관하는 우주 군사작전 연습인 ‘파트너 투 윈(Partner to Win)’에 처음 참가한다. 파트너 투 윈은 올해 신설한 국제 우주 워게임으로 우주에서 발생할 수 있는 여러 위기 상황에 대해 동맹·우방국 간 연합우주작전 수행 태세를 강화하려는 차원이다. 공군에 따르면 2∼6일 미 플로리다 올랜도에서 미 우주군 주관으로 열리는 워게임 ‘파트너 투 윈’에는 한미와 네덜란드 스웨덴 폴란드 브라질 등 6개국이 참가한다. 이번 워게임 참가는 손석락 공군참모총장이 올 2월 브래들리 솔츠먼 당시 미 우주군참모총장과의 통화에서 논의됐고, 이후 미 우주군이 양국 간 우주 협력 관계 강화를 위해 공군을 공식 초청하면서 성사됐다. 이번 워게임은 우주를 무대로 펼쳐질 수 있는 각종 위기 상황을 설정하고 각국 대표단이 대응과 공조 방안을...

items.title: 北, 사람 속여 침투 vs 美, AI로 돈줄 추적… 해킹 ‘창과 방패’ 전쟁
items.snippet: 지난달 29일(현지 시간) 세계 최대 가상자산 거래소 바이낸스에서 발생한 해킹 사건은 최근 북한과 미국이 벌이는 사이버전의 단면을 여실히 보여줬다는 평가가 나온다. 단일 해킹으로는 역대 최대 규모인 63억 달러(약 8조4000억 원)의 피해가 발생한 가운데, 북한 해커들은 바이낸스 관계자의 노트북에 악성코드를 심어 내부 시스템에 침투하는 이른바 ‘사람을 통한 해킹’ 전략을 구사한 것으로 알려졌다. 이에 맞서 미국은 인공지능(AI)과 블록체인 분석 등 첨단 기술을 활용해 자금 추적과 대응에 나섰다. 황석진 동국대 국제정보보호대학원 교수는 “북한이 내부 관계자의 기기를 이용해 해킹에 나서면 미국은 첨단 기술로 대응하는 일종의 ‘창과 방패’의 전쟁이 벌어지고 있는 것”이라며 “양측 모두 자신들에게 축적된 노하우와 강점을 앞세워 상대를 공략하는 상황...

items.title: 불안한 투자자들, 바이낸스 출금 재개 반나절만에 4.9조 인출
items.snippet: 세계 최대 가상자산 거래소 바이낸스가 북한 해킹 조직 ‘트레이더트레이터(TraderTraitor)’의 공격으로 63억 달러(약 8조4000억 원) 규모의 가상자산을 탈취당하며 일시 중단했던 자산 인출 거래를 1일(현지 시간) 재개했다. 바이낸스는 도난 자산의 약 95%에 해당하는 금액을 자체 자금으로 확보했다고 밝혔지만, 인출 재개 이후 약 9시간 반 만에 36억4000만 달러(약 4조9000억 원)의 자금이 순유출되는 등 이용자 불안이 여실히 드러났다. 이날 바이낸스는 X를 통해 “비트코인과 이더리움 등 일부 가상화폐의 인출을 재개했고, 보안 점검이 완료되는 대로 다른 자산 인출도 단계적으로 허용할 방침”이라고 밝혔다. 또 “탈취 자산의 약 95%를 자사 자산을 통해 충당했고, 나머지 5%는 시장 유동성이 부족해 확보하는 데 시간이 걸린다”...

items.title: 李 “가장 부정의했던 전두환이 정의사회 외쳐” 여권 강경파 겨냥
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령이 2일 “가장 부정의했던 전두환이 정의사회 구현을 외쳤다”면서 “정치적 올바름이 대중의 반발과 피로감에 부딪힌 이유는 언행불일치와 내로남불에 있다”고 지적했다. 선명성과 진보성을 앞세워 자신과 각을 세우고 있는 범여권 강경파 등에 대한 비판 발언을 닷새째 이어간 것. 탈이념적 이미지를 구축해 ‘구조적 다수’를 만들기 위한 지지층 확대를 시도하고 있다는 분석도 제기된다.● 李 “가장 부정의한 전두환이 정의사회 구현 외쳐” 이 대통령은 이날 오전 8시 7분 X(옛 트위터)에 올린 글에서 “정치적 올바름이 오늘날 대중의 반발과 피로감에 부딪힌 이유는 그 지향 가치 자체가 아니라 이를 주장하는 태도에 내재된 ‘언행불일치’와 ‘내로남불’에 있다”며 “위선과 이중잣대는 어떤 대의명분도 설득력을 잃게 만든다”고 적었다. 이어 “가장 부정의했...

items.title: 與, 오늘 의총서 신천지 조사결과 보고… 계파 전운
items.snippet: 더불어민주당이 3일 열리는 의원총회에서 김민석 대표가 8·17 전당대회 과정에서 제기한 ‘신천지 당원 가입 의혹’ 관련 조사 결과를 공유하기로 하면서 전운이 감돌고 있다. 당내에서 신천지 신도 수만 명의 가입 정황이 있다는 이야기가 나오는 가운데 친청(친정청래)계는 김 대표가 전당대회 과정에서 ‘반명(반이재명)·분열주의·신천지 3자 비밀 연합’이라고 거론한 근거 등을 문제 삼을 것으로 보인다. 2일 민주당에 따르면 3일 비공개 의총에는 신천지 당원 가입 여부에 대한 자체 조사 결과가 보고된다. 지난달 초 비공개 최고위에서 당원 정비 태스크포스(TF)를 맡은 박선원 최고위원이 조사 결과를 보고한 지 한 달여 만에 의원들에게 내용을 공개하는 것. 김 대표는 상당한 규모의 신천지 신도 집단 가입이 확인됐고 의미 있는 증언들도 축적했다고 밝힌 바 있...

items.title: 사람 못들어가는 ESS엔 CCTV 의무 없앤다
items.snippet: 정부가 사람이 들어갈 수 없는 컨테이너형 에너지저장장치(ESS)에 폐쇄회로(CC)TV 설치 의무를 없애는 방안을 추진한다. 규제합리화위원회와 국무총리 소속 민관합동 규제합리화추진단은 이 같은 내용의 ESS 설치·재활용 분야 개선 과제 12개가 확정됐다고 2일 밝혔다. 지금은 ESS를 설치한 장소 내부에는 사각지대가 생기지 않도록 CCTV를 설치해야 한다. 하지만 최근 통로가 없어 사람이 다닐 수 없는 컨테이너형 ESS가 늘고 CCTV보다 배터리 상태를 효과적으로 감시할 수 있는 배터리 관리 시스템(BMS)이 개발됨에 따라 CCTV 설치 의무를 완화하기로 했다. 정부는 연말까지 관련 위원회 심의를 거쳐 내년에는 관련 기후에너지환경부 고시인 ‘한국전기설비규정’ 개정을 추진할 계획이다. 하나의 컨테이너 내에 전기설비와 이차전지를 함께 설치할 수 없...

items.title: 해경, 내년 예산안 2.2조 편성… 中 불법조업 단속 함정 5척 확대
items.snippet: 국회가 본격적인 정부 예산안 심사에 돌입하는 가운데 해양경찰청은 2027년도 예산안으로 2조 2291억 원을 편성해 국회에 제출했다고 2일 밝혔다. 올해 예산(2조 885억 원) 대비 6.7% 증가한 규모다. 해경청은 ‘흔들림 없는 해양주권, 안전한 바다’를 목표로 국민이 체감할 수 있는 해양 안전 대책을 확보하는 데 중점을 두고 예산안을 편성했다고 설명했다. 주요 분야별로는 해양주권 수호에 5344억 원, 구조·안전에 1192억 원, 연구개발·정보화에 1160억 원 등을 각각 반영했다. 먼저 해경은 불법 조업 중국 어선에 강력 대응하기 위해 3000t급 경비함정 3척과 500t급 단속 전담 함정 2척의 건조 비용을 반영했다. 또 연안 사고 예방을 위해 감시에 활용할 연안순찰드론 22대, 동력구조보드 33대, 대형 스포츠유틸리티(SUV) 구조...

items.title: 제주, 마사회 등 공공기관 유치 전략 짠다

items.title: Israel's president begins process of coalition government negotiations
items.snippet: Israel's President Isaac Herzog begins the process of coalition government negotiations this week. One possibility is for the centrist opposition bloc to form a government with the Arab parties, which would oust current Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. items.title: 외국인 유학생 30만명 돌파… “이제 숫자 늘리기보다 교육의 질 높여야”
items.snippet: 국내 대학에서 공부하는 외국인 유학생이 올해 처음 30만명을 돌파했다. 정부는 2027년 유학생 30만명 유치를 목표로 다양한 정책을 펼쳐왔는데, 이를 1년 앞당겨 달성한 것이다. 이제 양적 확대뿐 아니라 유학생 교육의 질을 높이는 방향으로 나아가야 한다고 전문가들은 말한다. 교육부의 ‘2026년 교육기본통계 조사’ 결과에 따르면, 올해 국내 고등교육기관의 학위 및 비학위 과정에 등록돼 있는 유학생은 총 30만7464명이었다. 2024년 20만명을 넘은 이후 2년 만에 30만명을 돌파한 것이다.

items.title: [오늘의 날씨] 2026년 11월 3일
손님 끊긴 구둣방 새단장 후, 年 사용료 66% 올린다는 서울시
items.snippet: 지난 30일 오후 서울 지하철 2호선 역삼역 사거리는 직장인들로 붐볐다. 하지만 역 출구에 있는 구두 수선대는 한적했다. 수선대 앞을 오가는 직장인 대부분은 운동화를 신고 있었다. 25년째 이곳에서 구두를 닦아온 이상훈(66)씨는 “10여 년 전만 해도 하루 30~40켤레씩 닦았는데 요즘은 손님이 2~3명뿐”이라며 “구두만 닦아서는 먹고살 수 없어 오후 4시 30분이면 문을 닫고 밤마다 배달을 뛴다”고 했다.

items.title: 한국 6000만원 VS 미국 200억원
items.snippet: 2022년 12월 A씨는 전북 정읍시 한 국도에서 자전거를 끌고 걸어가다 시속 93㎞로 달리던 차량에 부딪혀 숨졌다. 이 도로의 제한 속도는 시속 60㎞였다. 법원은 작년 6월 사고 운전자에게 “위자료 총 6500만원을 유족에게 지급하라”고 판결했다. 재판부는 “운전자가 과속하지 않았다면 경미한 충격만 가했을 것”이라면서도 “야간에 야광 조끼 등 안전장치 없이 보행한 A씨에게도 일부 책임이 있다”고 했다.

items.title: “대통령, 대법관 후보 선정 개입은 안되고 대법원장도 대통령 판단 제한하면 안돼”
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령이 대법관 재(再)제청 논란과 관련해 헌법재판소에 의견서를 제출한 것으로 2일 확인됐다. 이 대통령 측은 의견서에서 “대통령의 임명권은 제청된 후보자를 임명하지 않을 권한을 포함한다” “대통령이 새 후보자 제청을 요청하는 것은 임명권의 본질이자 핵심”이라는 주장을 폈다. 장동혁 대표 등 국민의힘 의원 109명은 지난 9월 “이 대통령의 대법관 후보자 임명 동의안 미제출과 재제청 요구로 국회의 대법관 임명 동의권과 국회의원의 심의·표결권이 침해됐다”며 헌재에 권한쟁의심판을 청구했다. 이에 이 대통령 측은 21쪽 분량의 답변서를 지난달 13일 헌재에 제출했다.

items.title: 판사 80% “재판 중 AI 가짜판례 경험”
items.snippet: 현직 판사 10명 중 8명이 재판 과정에서 인공지능(AI)이 만든 가짜 판례가 담긴 서면을 받아본 적이 있는 것으로 2일 나타났다. 법원행정처가 지난달 각급 법원 법관 360명을 대상으로 실시한 AI 관련 설문 조사 결과다. 대법원이 공개한 조사 결과를 보면, 민사·가사·행정 담당 법관 중 약 80%가 잘못된 판례를 적용하거나 아예 없는 판례를 가짜로 만들어 인용한 사례를 경험했다고 답했다. 변호인 선임 비율이 높은 형사 담당 법관 등을 포함해 전체 응답자 중에선 67.5%가 이 같이 답했다. 유형별로는(복수 응답) 존재하지 않는 판례를 인용한 경우가 80.7%로 가장 많았고, 엉뚱한 판례를 인용한 경우 65.4%, 가짜 법령 인용 16.9% 등이 뒤를 이었다. 논문 등 AI가 만든 가짜 자료를 인용한 경우도 4.1%로 조사됐다.

items.title: 안전의 역설… 하청 챙길수록 ‘사용자’로 판정
items.snippet: 국내 건설사 현대엔지니어링은 올 6월 중앙노동위원회로부터 노란봉투법상 하청업체의 ‘진짜 사장’(사용자성)에 해당되는 만큼 하청 노조 요구대로 교섭에 응해야 한다는 통보를 받았다. 현대엔지니어링은 현행 산업안전보건법(산안법)에 따라 산업안전보건관리비를 책정하고 하청업체가 사용 계획을 제출하면 그 비용을 지급·감독하는 내용을 하청업체와의 계약서에 명시해 놓고 있었다. 또 현장 안전 관리 차원에서 안전 수칙을 위반한 하청 노동자를 작업에서 퇴출하는 제도를 운영하고, 일일 안전 회의를 진행해 왔다. 대부분 산안법상 의무를 이행하기 위한 안전 조치였지만, 중노위는 이를 사용자성 판단 근거로 삼았다.

items.title: [신문은 선생님] [사소한 역사] 비싼 설탕 대신 옥수수로 만든 ‘단맛’… 당분·열량 섭취 쉬워 비만 위험 커요
items.snippet: 의사들이 비만을 초래한다고 경고하는 대표적인 성분이 바로 액상과당입니다. 크림이 잔뜩 들어간 디저트, 지방이 가득한 음식과 달리, 액상과당은 주로 음료수에 들어 있어 시원하고 빠르게 섭취할 수 있어요. 하지만 액상과당이 들어 있는 달콤한 음료를 자주 마시면 당분과 열량을 지나치게 섭취하기 쉬워 비만 위험이 커질 수 있어요.

items.title: [신문은 선생님] [뉴스 고사성어] 다양한 요구 빗발친 프랑스 시위와 ‘중구난방’의 숨은 뜻
items.snippet: 무리 중(衆) 입 구(口) 어려울 난(難) 막을 방(防) 프랑스가 시위로 몸살을 앓고 있습니다. 학생들이 학습 환경 개선을 요구하며 시작했는데, 다양한 이가 참가한 후 폭력으로 번져 상점 약탈과 방화도 잇따르고 있어요. 교육 여건 개선, 물가와 연료비 인하, 복지 예산 요구, 공무원 임금 동결 반대까지 사회 각계의 목소리가 뒤섞인 상황입니다. 여러 분야에서 각기 제 주장을 하느라 통제가 어려운 상황이 됐습니다. 이럴 때 어울리는 말이 ‘뭇사람의 입은 막기 어렵다’는 뜻의 중구난방입니다. 중구난방의 현재 뜻은 여럿이 저마다 떠들어 갈피를 잡기 어려운 상황을 가리키지만, 본래는 여론은 억누른다고 사라지지 않는다는 뜻이었습니다.

items.title: [신문은 선생님] [재미있는 과학] 에스컬레이터 한 줄 서기, 편마모가 기계 고장 부추겨요
items.snippet: 빼빼로 과자를 주고받는 날로 널리 알려진 11월 11일. 사실 이날은 ‘승강기 안전의 날’이기도 합니다. 승강기는 엘리베이터와 에스컬레이터 등 동력을 사용해 사람이나 화물을 위아래로 나르는 장치를 말하는데요. 행정안전부와 한국승강기안전공단은 매년 기념식을 열고, 안전한 승강기 사용에 대한 홍보를 합니다. 또 영상, 포스터 등 공모전을 진행하는데, 에스컬레이터에서 뛰거나 걷지 말자는 내용이 많이 담깁니다. 그런데 과연 우리는 에스컬레이터를 얼마나 안전하게 이용하고 있는 걸까요? 지하철역에서 에스컬레이터를 타다 보면 익숙한 풍경이 눈에 들어와요. 오른쪽에는 사람들이 빽빽하게 서 있고, 왼쪽은 바쁜 사람들을 위해 비워두고 있죠. 이를 ‘한 줄 서기’라고 해요. 그런데 과연 한 줄로 서고 다른 줄을 비워두는 게 미덕일까요? 아니면 양쪽에 나란히 서는...

items.title: “포퓰리즘 버리고 국익 택한 獨 총리들… 우리도 과감한 결단 내릴 지도자 절실”
items.snippet: 김황식 전 총리와 독일의 인연은 각별하다. 서른 살이던 1978년 마르부르크 대학교에서 1년간 독일 민법을 배웠고, 총리로 퇴임한 2013년 다시 베를린자유대학으로 건너가 독일의 정치와 법 제도를 공부했다. 그의 40년 공직 생활의 화두는 ‘독일’. “같은 분단 국가였는데 독일과 한반도의 오늘은 왜 다를까?”를 파고든 그는 ‘독일의 힘, 독일의 총리들’이란 책으로 그 해법을 제시하기도 했다.

items.title: Visualizing Anisotropic Charge Transport in CrSBr using Bias-Dependent Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy
items.abstract: Anisotropic semiconductors offer unique opportunities for next-generation electronics due to their direction-dependent transport. However, conventional electrical measurements provide only spatially averaged characteristics. Here, we employ bias-dependent Kelvin probe force microscopy (KPFM) to directly visualize the response of CrSBr under different electrical bias configurations. Spatially resolved KPFM maps reveal highly distinct, crystallographic-direction-dependent potential profiles. To elucidate this behavior, we employ anisotropic transport simulations that capture the charge transport and electric-field distributions in CrSBr. The close agreement between experiment and simulation provides a unified picture of anisotropic charge transport and bias-induced potential redistribution. Our experiments further reveal a boundary-associated redistribution of the transport field when bias...

items.title: Streaming Virtual Metrology via Lightweight Adaptation under Temporal Distribution Shifts
items.abstract: Virtual metrology (VM) aims to estimate costly or delayed metrology variables from heterogeneous sensor signals and in-line measurements, and it acts as a critical component of semiconductor manufacturing. While recent data-driven models have improved VM accuracy, most are trained in batch settings and assume stationary data distributions. items.title: A Mixed-Precision CNN-LSTM Accelerator Featuring Long-Kernel Memory Reuse and Dynamic Quantization for Sleep Staging
items.abstract: This letter presents a mixed-precision CNN-LSTM accelerator for EEG-based sleep staging. To efficiently execute long temporal convolutions, a serpentine dataflow propagates activations between neighboring processing elements, reducing memory accesses by 6.2 times and 2.25 times compared with output- and weight-stationary dataflows, respectively. A hybrid quantization scheme applies runtime dynamic quantization to the LSTM and MLP layers and assigns mixed precision on a layer-by-layer basis, reducing model size by 4.16 times. Combined with a bit-flexible MAC architecture and channel-grouped memory scheduling, the accelerator supports INT2/4/8/16 inference. Fabricated in 65 nm CMOS, the accelerator consumes 0.40 mW and achieves a 258 times speedup over an iso-frequency 32b RISC-V processor. Evaluated across all 62 subjects in the public MASS-SS3 dataset using 31-fold leave-two-subject-out...

Grazing-incidence X-ray diffraction reveals reduced peak broadening, a smaller lattice parameter, and a stronger (111) preferred orientation with increasing annealing temperature. items.abstract: This paper proposes an open-source automated LC matching network optimization framework that combines schematic-level design optimization with electromagnetic (EM)-aware post-layout refinement. An ML-based surrogate predicts the frequency-dependent complex admittance of individual routes, enabling reuse across matching network topologies and physical layouts for the same technology node without retraining. These route models guide post-layout passive retuning to recover matching performance while preserving the layout footprint. items.abstract: The SuperCDMS experiment uses semiconductor crystal detectors operated at cryogenic temperatures to search for low-mass dark matter. Vibrations observed during the SuperCDMS Soudan experiment generated broadband low-frequency noise (LFN), which due to its similarity in the pulse shape to the low-energy signal events is difficult to remove. In the final low ionization threshold analysis, CDMSlite Run 3, the strong event selection criterion applied to remove LFN events also significantly reduced the ability to identify signal events in the low energy region, thus reducing the sensitivity of the experiment to low-mass dark matter. Therefore, an LFN rejection criterion using machine learning (ML) aimed to improve the signal efficiency while maintaining the signal purity has now been developed. items.title: Field-resolved observation and quantification of the instantaneous Kerr response in semiconductors
items.abstract: The optical Kerr effect, whereby the refractive index of a material changes with light intensity, underpins nonlinear photonics and emerging mid-infrared technologies. Accurate determination of the nonlinear refractive index is therefore essential, yet conventional intensity-based techniques infer the nonlinear phase shift indirectly from changes in beam propagation or optical spectra. Moreover, methods such as the $z$-scan cannot resolve the temporal evolution of the nonlinear response, making it difficult to distinguish instantaneous Kerr nonlinearities from delayed contributions, including free-carrier effects. Here, we investigate the nonlinear optical response of germanium at $5 μ\mathrm{m}$ using field-resolved degenerate pump-probe spectroscopy. items.title: “해외에서 엄마 김치 먹고 싶은 분?”… 시골 우체국이 살아남는 법
items.snippet: ‘백수’ 우체국이 새 일자리를 찾았다. 전남광주 영광군 백수읍에 있는 우체국 이야기다. 이 우체국은 인구 감소로 우편물이 줄어 새로운 활로가 절실한 상황이었다. 눈을 해외로 돌렸다. 김장철인 지난해 12월, SNS에 ‘엄마 김치가 그리운 해외 교민들의 김치 배송을 돕겠다’는 글을 올렸다. 이른바 ‘김치 해외 배송 대행’이다. 과정은 이렇다. 백수우체국에 신청하면 집으로 김치를 담을 수 있는 금속 용기(캔)를 보내준다. 여기에 김치를 담아 백수우체국으로 보내면 된다. 나머지는 우체국 직원들이 알아서 한다. 김치캔을 보랭 상자에 넣고 산소·발효 가스 흡수제와 보랭 팩 등을 추가해 재포장한 뒤 국제특급우편(EMS)으로 원하는 해외 주소에 발송해 준다. 소비자는 EMS 요금만 내면 된다.

items.title: Full-Potential Korringa Kohn Rostoker Study of Structural and Mechanical Properties in SiGeSn Alloys
items.abstract: Accurate first-principles descriptions of open, covalently bonded crystal structures remain challenging within conventional Korringa--Kohn--Rostoker (KKR) approaches owing to the spherical approximations commonly employed for the effective crystal potential. Here, we systematically assess the recently developed full-potential KKR (KKR-FP) implementation in the open-source MuST package and demonstrate its applicability to diamond-structured group-IV semiconductors and SiGeSn alloys. Benchmark calculations for diamond-structured Si reveal substantial limitations of the conventional muffin-tin and atomic sphere approximations, whereas KKR-FP accurately reproduces the experimental equilibrium lattice parameter and bulk modulus, yielding 5.433 and 94.9 GPa. items.title: Dipolar Exciton Polarons in a van der Waals Homobilayer
items.abstract: Fermi polarons exemplify how many-body interactions give rise to emergent quasiparticles, providing a fundamental framework for understanding interacting quantum matter. In electron-doped two-dimensional semiconductors, exciton polarons offer optical access to Fermi-polaron physics and electrical tunability, yet achieving stronger and more controllable exciton-electron interactions remains a key challenge. Here, we realize dipolar exciton polarons in an electrically tunable van der Waals homobilayer, where interlayer excitons with spatially separated electrons and holes act as quantum impurities carrying permanent electric dipole moments. These dipolar polarons exhibit substantially enhanced exciton-electron interactions, with binding energies more than four times those of conventional intralayer exciton polarons. items.title: Photonic Crystal Integrated Graphene-Silicon Schottky Diodes for Resonant Infrared Photodetection
items.abstract: Narrowband infrared (IR) photodetection has become a critical technology for the next generation of smart low-power photodetectors. In this work, we present a device based on a graphene-silicon Schottky junction with narrowband response in the short-wave IR (SWIR) regime. Integrating a photonic crystal (PhC) slab in the device enables a wavelength dependant tailoring of graphene absorption. The devices were characterized by photocurrent measurement, which was enhanced more than two orders of magnitude by the PhC integration. The sharp enhancements obtained can also be predicted by numerical simulation. This approach offers a highly scalable, tunable, CMOS-compatible architecture for narrowband IR photodetection, paving the way for next-generation, low-power IR sensors.

In this contribution, we evaluated ILGAD sensors bump-bonded to 25 μm pitch charge-integrating MÖNCH chips at a laser-driven soft X-ray source. items.title: Y2CdX4 (X = S, Se, Te) Semiconductors: A First-Principles Study of Structural, Electronic, Optical, and Energy-Related Properties
items.abstract: We present a comprehensive density functional theory (DFT) investigation of the structural, mechanical, electronic, optical, thermoelectric, and bonding properties of Y2CdX4 (X = S, Se, Te) compounds for potential optoelectronic and energy-conversion applications. Structural optimization reveals a systematic expansion of the equilibrium lattice parameters from S to Te. The calculated bulk moduli decrease from 83 GPa for Y2CdS4 to 68 GPa for Y2CdSe4 and 54 GPa for Y2CdTe4, indicating progressive lattice softening. Electronic band-structure calculations predict indirect band gaps of 2.42, 2.08, and 1.71 eV for Y2CdS4, Y2CdSe4, and Y2CdTe4, respectively, with further narrowing upon inclusion of spin-orbit coupling. items.title: Universal model of the growth of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors on polar surfaces: pyramids and glue atoms. II. Adsorption of nonmetal atoms (N, P, As, and Sb) on Ga-terminated surfaces
items.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to simulate the adsorption processes on Ga-terminated surfaces of tetrahedral semiconductors: GaN, GaP, GaAs and GaSb. The considered adsorbates are nonmetal species, i.e., nitrogen, phosphorus, arsenic, and antimony on wurtzite gallium nitride, i.e., GaN(0001) surfaces, zinc blende gallium phosphide, i.e., GaP(111), gallium arsenide, GaAs(111), and gallium antimonide, GaSb (111) surfaces. The cases investigated include single adsorbed nonmetal atoms and full coverage, i.e. theta=1 of these surfaces. The calculated results include the stable sites and the energies of the single adsorbed atoms: located at H3 sites at low coverage and in on-top positions at high coverage for GaP, GaAs and GaSb. items.abstract: Ab initio calculations were used to elucidate the properties of the polar surfaces of III-V tetrahedral semiconductors, i.e., metal- and nonmetal-terminated. The systems considered were clean wurtzite gallium nitride (i.e. (0001) and (000-1) GaN surfaces), zinc blende gallium phosphide (i.e. (111) and (-1-1-1) GaP), gallium arsenide (i.e. (111) and (-1-1-1) GaAs), and (111) and (-1-1-1) GaSb surfaces. The calculated data include the crystallographic structure and the electronic states of the termination atoms on both sides, i.e. their positions, energies, and occupations. All nonmetal-terminated surfaces exhibit no reconstruction, and their broken-bond states are located in the vicinity of the valence band maxima (VBM), pinning the Fermi level. items.title: Quantifying Blinking Suppression and Probing Its Mechanism in PPD-Treated Single Quantum Dots
items.abstract: Colloidal semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) are highly promising materials for various applications, yet photoluminescence intermittency (blinking) remains a key obstacle to their practical use. While recent advances have enabled partial or complete suppression of this effect, both the degree of suppression and the mechanism by which it occurs are often difficult to establish. In the present work we analyse the blinking suppression of single CdSe/ZnS QDs after treatment with p-phenylenediamine (PPD), recently discovered by Yang et al. We revisit the blinking mechanism in this system and show that it is governed predominantly by the trapping mechanism, rather than by Auger ionization as previously proposed. items.title: FrontierMat: Benchmarking Language Models at the Frontier of Materials R&D
items.abstract: To accelerate materials discovery, language models must be able to address problems at the research frontier. Yet textbook- and examination-derived benchmarks primarily assess established knowledge, leaving performance on frontier research problems largely untested. We introduce FrontierMat, a benchmark of 330 problems drawn from frontier academic and industrial research in fields including aerospace, semiconductors, embodied intelligence and nuclear fusion. Every problem is validated by leading experimentalists and industry experts in its field. Each problem presents a real study and asks the model to infer a withheld outcome or draw a conclusion from selected experimental evidence. Problems are annotated by functional domain, material system and the scale of the governing mechanism; 130 require cross-scale reasoning. items.title: Unifying dynamical electron-electron and electron-phonon interactions from first principles
items.abstract: Electron-phonon interactions in materials with free carriers are dynamically screened by low-energy electronic excitations, yet first-principles calculations almost always treat this screening in the adiabatic approximation. A fully dynamical treatment of metals and doped semiconductors within time-dependent density functional perturbation theory (TDDFPT) is expensive and numerically delicate. Here, we introduce DFPT+A downfolding ("A" for active space), which starts from the static density functional perturbation theory (DFPT) response of a computationally convenient base system and adds the dynamical screening of a low-energy active space, described by Wannier functions. The required statically screened electron-electron interaction is computed using DFPT directly in the basis of Wannier-function pairs and truncated in a computationally efficient and systematically improvable way. items.abstract: Untrusted third-party entities throughout the semiconductor supply chain expose proprietary hardware intellectual property to reverse engineering, piracy, and overproduction. While logic locking counters this threat by embedding key-dependent logic, conventional static key-gates remain vulnerable to both oracle-guided SAT attacks and structural removal attacks due to their time-invariant netlist signatures. items.abstract: $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ photoconductive semiconductor switches (PCSSs) are attractive for high-voltage operation, but above-bandgap triggering requires deep-ultraviolet excitation. Here, we investigate a 650-um-thick, 0.01% Fe-doped $β$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ impurity PCSS with a 5-mm lateral gap under continuous-wave (CW) 808-nm sub-bandgap excitation at biases up to 10 kV ( 20 kV cm^-1). The device exhibited clear sub-bandgap photoconductive switching. As the optical power density increased from 0.64 to 3.18 W cm^-2, the ON-state current increased progressively while the ON-state resistance decreased, consistent with enhanced defect-assisted photocarrier generation. A higher applied bias further strengthened the switching response through enhanced field-assisted carrier transport. items.title: Complete Au-free Metallization Platform for UWBG Al$_{0.65}$Ga$_{0.35}$N channel MOS-HEMTs using Ti/Al/Ti Ohmic Contacts and Refractory TiN/Pt Gates
items.abstract: Au-free ohmic contacts and refractory gate stacks are critical for integrating ultra-wide-bandgap (UWBG) Al-rich AlGaN transistors with Si-CMOS technology. In this work, we demonstrate, to our knowledge, the first complete Au-free metallization platform for Al$_{0.65}$Ga$_{0.35}$N-channel MOS-HEMTs, combining electron-beam-evaporated and sputtered Ti/Al/Ti ohmic contacts with sputtered TiN and Pt gate metals. The Ti/Al/Ti contacts achieved a contact resistance of approximately 7.5--7.7 $Ω\cdot$mm while being fully Au-free. This contact resistance is achieved using a 600 $^\circ$C anneal, substantially below the 850--950 $^\circ$C typically required for Au-capped Ti/Al/X/Au contacts on Al-rich AlGaN, indicating a reduced thermal budget and improved compatibility with silicon-CMOS foundries. items.title: Efficient Simulation of Gate Leakage Currents in Ultra-scaled Transistors from First Principles
items.abstract: To ensure high electrostatic integrity in ultra-scaled field-effect transistors (FETs), thin gate dielectric layers are typically needed, potentially giving rise to (strong) leakage currents. Being able to model this effect is therefore crucial. Here, we show how gate leakage currents can be computed at the ab initio level in WS$_2$-hBN FETs by extending the well-established quantum transmitting boundary method (QTBM). Two main challenges are tackled: (i) the calculation of the open boundary conditions (OBCs) for the gate contacts and (ii) the solution of the resulting sparse linear system of equations A x = b where the matrix A possesses an unstructured sparsity pattern. We demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the state of the art and can be readily applied to simulate transistors with gate lengths exceeding 25 nm.

items.title: Electric field control of anisotropic spin traffic between spin-filtering and magnon-scattering in a layered antiferromagnet
items.abstract: Layered A-type antiferromagnetic (AFM) semiconductors offer a unique platform for spintronic devices by combining robust magnetism with gate-tunable semiconducting properties. We present a dual-gate field-effect transistor based on CrSBr, a layered A-type AFM with pronounced transport anisotropy and complex spin dynamics. Our device provides independent control over carrier density and displacement field. Systematic transport measurements reveal that the displacement field, rather than doping, predominantly governs the sign and magnitude of magnetoresistance ratio (MRR). We identify the origins of both negative and positive MRR components and connect them to interlayer and intralayer spin-dependent transport mechanisms. We interpret these findings with ab initio calculations and an effective spin-circuit model that reproduces the anisotropic magnetotransport. Our results identify the dis...

items.title: Uncertainty-aware Feedback Loop Diagnosis: integrating reinforcement learning and conformal prediction for reliable wafer defect classification
items.abstract: Semiconductor manufacturing is a complex, multi-step process that requires both high precision and low operating costs. Therefore, detecting defects in a high-volume setting is an important component of wafer map analysis for reliable production. However, most state-of-the-art deep learning approaches require a full scan of the surface, which hinders the development of high-throughput inspection systems. To address this problem, we propose Uncertainty-aware Feedback Loop Diagnosis (UFLD), a novel algorithm that employs reinforcement learning for adaptive measurement acquisition and provides a prediction uncertainty level after each step, stopping the process once sufficient information is obtained. items.abstract: Alloying offers a convenient route to tune the physical properties of semiconductors, at the price, however, of local lattice/bond distortions needed to accommodate the lattice mismatch. items.title: Electronic liquid crystals and superconductivity from doping a moiré Mott insulator
items.abstract: Electronic liquid crystals, such as stripe phases and nematics, are self-organized states of matter with spontaneously broken rotational symmetry. They are expected to emerge in a doped Mott insulator as a compromise between short- and long-range Coulomb interactions, and are believed to be intimately connected to the emergence of high temperature superconductivity either as a competing order or an intertwined order. Moiré semiconductors provide a controllable platform to explore the relationship between stripe phases and superconductivity near a Mott insulator. Here we report the generic appearance of stripe phases in a doped moiré Mott insulator and the observation of a stripe to-superconductor quantum phase transition in twisted bilayer WSe2. items.abstract: Controlling the number n of connected octahedra layers in two-dimensional metal halide perovskites enables fine control of the semiconductor band gap that is highly advantageous for optoelectronic and light emission applications. Phase purity in terms of n is crucial towards narrow emission bands and the design of band structure alignment for charge carrier funneling. We present a simple and scalable synthesis method using cesium and butylammonium as A-cations to fabricate microcrystal powders of 2D lead bromide perovskites that results in samples with very high n-phase purity. The obtained microcrystals show a sharp onset in absorbance and single narrow emission peak in UV-blue spectral range, and we confirm their structure and composition with X-ray diffraction and energy dispersive spectroscopy. items.title: SKFitter: Symmetry resolved Slater Koster tight-binding models from first principles for s, p, d and f electrons, spin orbit coupling and magnetism
items.abstract: Constructing accurate and physically interpretable tight binding (TB) Hamiltonians from first principles calculations remains challenging, particularly for materials exhibiting complex orbital hybridization, spin orbit coupling (SOC), and magnetic order. SKFitter is an open-source Python framework for constructing and optimizing symmetry resolved Slater Koster TB models directly from density functional theory (DFT) calculations performed using Quantum ESPRESSO or VASP. The framework supports s to f orbitals, incorporates on site SOC and site resolved magnetic exchange interactions, and accommodates both orthogonal and nonorthogonal basis. A central feature is the symmetry resolved parameterization of orbital manifolds, which allows independent two centre hopping integrals between symmetry allowed orbital groups and across distinct neighbour shells. items.title: PDE-based Bayesian Inverse Problems in All-at-once Framework
items.abstract: We propose a modern all-at-once framework for PDE-based Bayesian inversion by introducing the PDE residual as probabilistic information. In this framework, the PDE residual is treated as a soft constraint with a residual covariance and is directly incorporated into the likelihood function. The new hybrid likelihood function eliminates PDE solves, thus reducing expensive computational costs, while performing rigorous Bayesian inference. Theoretically, we establish the well-posedness of the posterior with uncertainty quantification, and numerically, we propose two efficiency inversion algorithms based on two posterior sampling methods. In particular, one algorithm is based on Metropolis-within-Gibbs MCMC method with a PDE-informed block- diagonal Gaussian prior, and the other is based on a joint sampling strategy. This is true for a wide range of shell thickness, from about one monolayer, up to 25 nm thanks to the good lattice match between the InAs material of the core and the ZnTe material of the shell. While (1 100) m-facets and (11 20) a-facets coexist on the sidewalls of the core, during the growth of the ZnTe shell the size of the m-facets progressively increases at the expense of the a-facets which eventually disappear. items.title: I$_4$ complex acting as near-infrared emitter with a quantum memory in silicon
items.abstract: Silicon color centers emitting in the near infrared offer a route to spin--photon interfaces compatible with mature complementary metal--oxide--semiconductor fabrication. A key unresolved candidate is the X-line at 1039.7 meV in the photoluminescence (PL) spectrum, long attributed to a complex of four self-interstitials (I$_4$), yet whose microscopic structure and spin properties have remained controversial and uncharacterized at a predictive level. Using hybrid-functional (HSE06) density functional theory, we unambiguously establish the bare I$_4$ complex as the origin of the X-line: our calculations quantitatively reproduce the zero-phonon line, the complete phonon sideband structure---identifying the prominent secondary peaks as one- and two-phonon replicas of strongly coupled quasi-local modes---and the EPR hyperfine constants. items.title: Implementation and Validation of Mismatch-Tolerant High-Gain OTA with a Calibrated Negative Conductance Load
items.abstract: This paper presents the circuit-level implementation of a mismatch-tolerant high-gain operational transconductance amplifier (OTA) using automatic negative-conductance calibration in 65-nm CMOS. The technique enhances OTA gain by compensating for its finite output conductance using a cross-coupled transistor pair, with an on-chip calibration loop that eliminates the need for a replica circuit or external tuning. The calibration routine increases the gain by driving the steady state error of the OTA in a unity gain feedback loop toward zero. The implementation addresses practical challenges involving comparator offset, DAC design, and subtractor gain and offset. A 6-bit capacitive DAC (CDAC)-based comparator offset calibration scheme enables reliable detection of the sub-millivolt steady state error required for high OTA gain. items.title: OPERA: OPamp Design by an Expert-Taught Reasoning Agent, from Specifications to Layout
items.abstract: Analog flows from specifications to a signed-off layout rarely run without manual iteration. Recent large language model (LLM) agents size circuits with optimizer loops over the device dimensions and stop at the schematic. We present OPERA (OPamp design by an Expert-taught Reasoning Agent), in which a general-purpose LLM agent designs CMOS opamps from specifications to post-layout sign-off with open-source tools. First, the designer teaches the agent the gm/ID method: map the specifications to transconductances and minimum currents, choose gm/ID per device role from characterized lookup tables, and size from equations, leaving a few knobs to search and an explainable design. Second, the agent learns the gLayout framework and taught layout practice, and writes a reusable layout generator that closes the layout and extraction loop at designer-approved gates. items.title: Characterizing Performance Tradeoffs in Heterogeneous GPU-Wafer-Scale Accelerator Systems
items.abstract: As AI accelerator architectures become increasingly diverse, integrating different architectures into a unified system is emerging as a new heterogeneous computing paradigm. GPUs and WSEs differ substantially in compute, memory, and communication organization, creating both architectural complementarity and additional overheads, yet how to translate this heterogeneity into practical performance gains remains unclear. To address this gap, we propose a hierarchical benchmarking methodology to characterize GPU--WSE heterogeneous execution and the conditions for exploiting complementarity, together with an analytical performance model that identifies when heterogeneity becomes a bottleneck and when it yields system-level performance gains.

items.title: Colossal magnetoresistance in narrow-gap magnetic semiconductor Eu$_2$CdAs$_2$
items.abstract: Discovering antiferromagnetic materials with a sizable colossal magnetoresistance (CMR) effect and precisely tuning their responses remain significant challenges in materials science. This work reports the synthesis, phase transitions, and magnetotransport properties of the narrow-gap Zintl arsenide Eu$_2$CdAs$_2$. The compound undergoes antiferromagnetic ordering at $T_\mathrm{N} = 9$ K and exhibits semiconducting behavior with a low-temperature activation energy of 3.2 meV, achieving a large CMR effect of $-10^4\%$ at 9 T. Below $T_\mathrm{N}$, a distinct butterfly-shaped magnetoresistance hysteresis emerges without any macroscopic ferromagnetic order, revealing a transport anomaly likely dictated by AFM domain dynamics and/or the formation and percolation of localized magnetic polarons. items.title: Lone-Pair Stereoactivity Overrides Mass Scaling of Thermal Expansion and Heat Conduction in Non-vander Waals Layered Bismuth Oxychalcogenides
items.abstract: Heavier chalcogens are generally expected to soften isostructural semiconductor lattices, raising thermal expansion and lowering thermal conductivity. Layered bismuth oxychalcogenides, Bi2O2X (X = S, Se, Te), are mixed-anion crystals whose covalent slabs and ionic sheets are bound electrostatically rather than by van der Waals forces and whose Bi3+ 6s^2 lone pairs can become stereochemically active. Despite the rapid development of Bi2O2Se for fin and gate-all-around transistors, its fundamental thermal expansion and heat transport mechanisms remain poorly understood. items.title: Numerical schemes for 1D capacitively coupled plasma fluid simulation
items.abstract: Capacitively coupled plasmas (CCP) are widely used in semiconductor manufacturing, where fluid models provide an efficient approach to the simulation of the low-temperature discharge. The model considered in this work couples the electron and the ion continuity equations, the electron energy equation and the Poisson's equation for the electric potential. We investigate the numerical schemes for the simulation of the 1D-CCP. In particular, a semi-implicit Scharfetter-Gummel (SG) scheme is adopted for the Poisson's equation, while the remaining equations are solved using the implicit SG schemes. The proposed strategy can be naturally extended to the 2D cases. Several alternative schemes are also discussed and tested. Numerical experiments compare these methods in terms of the admissible time step $Δt$, total simulation time, accuracy against a reference solution and robustness of the schem...

items.title: Volumetric Nanophotonics for Enhanced Scintillation and Remote Light Outcoupling
items.abstract: Nanophotonic patterning is a promising approach to enhancing light extraction in scintillator materials, with the potential to improve performance in applications such as medical imaging and particle detection. While 2D surface patterns have been successful in improving scintillator performance, the true potential of nanophotonic patterning lies in the bulk, where photons are emitted, transported, and absorbed. Here, we experimentally demonstrate the enhancement and control of scintillation using 2.5D volumetric nanophotonic patterns. Using a direct femtosecond laser writing approach, we nanofabricate square lattices of air holes into the bulk of inorganic scintillators (YAG:Ce and YAG:Yb), achieving nearly subwavelength periods compared to the peak emission wavelength and depths up to hundreds of microns, which fill a large fraction of the full thickness of the bulk. items.title: A Case Study of a Multi-Agent Kernel-Optimization Loop That Learns a New AI Accelerator
items.abstract: Frontier large language models write correct CUDA kernels for most single-operator benchmark tasks, yet their accuracy collapses on accelerators whose architecture and programming language they have rarely seen. We present a case study of an LLM agent loop built for such accelerators. Our example is the FuriosaAI RNGD NPU, programmed in a recent, sparsely documented Rust DSL, where the loop optimized three Gemma-4-12B decode kernels over 12 days on a shared, scarce device. The loop builds its own target knowledge: it writes and checks a summary of the DSL documentation, measures the chip with microbenchmarks, records compiler-derived legality rules, and revisits this knowledge when the toolchain changes, rechecking rules and measurements where it can. items.abstract: Design-based metrology of academic electron beam lithography (EBL) is bottlenecked by low-throughput imaging. For integrated photonics, where nanometre-scale structural variation can significantly limit device performance, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) is the standard tool for critical dimension (CD) metrology, revealing the structure of devices that is not available from optical measurements. Manual SEM imaging on a wafer-scale is time-intensive, can feature operator-dependent distortions, and yields too few data to reliably close the nanofabrication calibration loop. The following details a methodology that utilises existing hardware in an academic cleanroom: a GDSII-to-SEM software workflow that converts a facility's superseded pattern generator into a CD-SEM for unattended image acquisition and efficient CD and line edge roughness (LER) extraction. items.title: Coherent control and high purity single-photon emission from telecom quantum dots on metamorphic InGaAs
items.abstract: Semiconductor quantum dots emitting in the telecommunication O- and C-bands are promising candidates as single-photon sources for fiber-based quantum communication. In this work, we show how coherent quasi-resonant and phonon-assisted excitation help reveal the intrinsic optical properties of InAs quantum dots embedded in relaxed InGaAs matrices on top of metamorphic InGaAs layers for achieving emission in the telecom bands. By systematically comparing excitation schemes, we separate excitation-induced effects from intrinsic emitter properties. This allows us to observe linewidths as narrow as 21 $μ$eV, the disappearance of slow decay channels, and single-photon purity reaching second-order autocorrelation values in the order of $10^{-2}$. items.title: Parity-Resolved Many-Body Kinetics of a Topological Qubit under Nonequilibrium Phonon Pulses
items.abstract: Phonon bursts from ionizing radiation cause correlated errors in superconducting quantum processors. We study prescribed nonequilibrium phonon pulses in a Majorana qubit formed by two $2\,μ\mathrm{m}$ proximitized nanowires. Combining the lattice Lutchyn--Oreg model, microscopic electron--phonon coupling, and parity-resolved many-body dynamics, we track excitation, relaxation, and logical coherence. Without quasiparticle escape, recombination restores the initial Majorana occupations in about 130 ns, while phonons exchanged during excitation and recovery can retain logical-state information, leaving permanent coherence loss. For mirror-symmetric wires, the fractional coherence loss per wire is 0.75--1.0 times the excitation probability averaged over the two logical states, even at zero Majorana splitting; breaking mirror symmetry can suppress dephasing at small splitting. items.title: A Fast and Memory-Efficient Algorithm for Searching Faint Moving Objects using Synthetic Tracking
items.abstract: Detecting unknown faint moving objects using optical imaging is challenging. Long exposure times are infeasible for such targets, as the resulting image streaking causes a loss of signal-to-noise ratio due to energy dispersal across multiple pixels. To address this, synthetic tracking, a track-before-detect method, replaces long exposures with many short exposures, integrating them in post-processing to recover the moving signal. Enabled by modern CMOS detectors with fast readout and low read noise, this technique synthesizes telescope tracking by searching over a grid of velocities. However, the conventional brute-force implementation imposes a significant computational burden: integrating N_f frames of size (N_x,N_y) requires O(N_x N_y N_f^3) operations. items.title: Back-End-Of-Line Integration of 2-Terminal Ferroelectric Hafnia Synaptic Weights on Commercial CMOS Process
items.abstract: Functionalising the back-end-of-line (BEOL) of CMOS with emerging materials is a key route to neural network accelerators and neuromorphic systems. In this work, we demonstrate for the first time the integration of 2-terminal ferroelectric synaptic weights in the BEOL of as-delivered commercial 180 nm CMOS dies. A novel material stack is proposed, in which a WOx/[HfO2-ZrO2] bilayer is sandwiched between TiN and Mo electrodes. For devices annealed at 450 °C, programming below 1.8 V is achieved with a cycle-to-cycle variation below 3 %. Synaptic weights annealed at 500 °C exhibit more gradual weight updates, while the tested underlying NMOS transistors remain functional after the complete integration process. The trade-off between thermal budget and on-device training performance is illustrated using hardware-aware neural network simulations.

items.title: Prospector: learning a compact graph traversal policy for scientific reasoning
items.abstract: Scientific reasoning in specialized engineering fields depends on knowledge scattered across the literature, often proprietary and absent from frontier LLM training data. In such domains, frontier models tend to give generic answers. Knowledge graphs (KGs) can ground LLM reasoning. Because a graph is too large to provide in full, typical LLM+KG systems preselect a portion, deciding relevance before reasoning begins. Here we train a compact model, Prospector, to reason over a domain knowledge graph by traversing it step by step, seeking evidence in light of what it has already found. Prospector calls a small set of tools one at a time to progressively build its context, and answers with a chain of evidence that can be checked edge by edge against what its tools retrieved from the graph. items.abstract: Spintronic terahertz (THz) emitters based on ferromagnet/heavy-metal bilayers provide an efficient route for generating broadband THz radiation through ultrafast spin-to-charge conversion. However, Ni/Pt bilayers usually exhibit relatively weak THz emission, limiting their use as efficient spintronic emitters. Here, we report an interface-assisted enhancement of THz emission in ZnO/Ni/Pt heterostructures. By placing ZnO underneath Ni while preserving the direct Ni/Pt contact, the THz amplitude is increased by up to approximately 2.8 times compared with the Ni/Pt reference. The enhanced emission reverses polarity with the magnetic field and follows the expected angular dependence of ultrafast spin-to-charge conversion. items.title: Machine Learning Hamiltonians with Polarizations for Heterogeneous Systems
items.abstract: Machine learning Hamiltonians use local atomic structures to determine local Hamiltonian matrix elements without carrying out self-consistent calculations. They have been used to study large systems and to carry out high-throughput screening for their electronic and optical properties. The prediction of the Hamiltonian is essentially the prediction of the electron electrostatic potential energy; however, for heterogeneous systems, this potential energy is often determined by faraway features, such as interface or surface dipoles, or even an applied voltage in a nanodevice. Thus, it cannot be determined by local atomic structures alone. In this sense, one needs to solve the electron electrostatic potential energy self-consistently using intrinsic atomic dipoles, the applied external potential energy, and polarizabilities. Fortunately, the intrinsic dipoles and polarizabilities are local p...

items.title: Demonstration of high output power (3.75 W/mm) with 31.8% PAE in Ga-Polar AlGaN/GaN HEMTs on sapphire at 94 GHz
items.abstract: In this work, a recessed-gate Ga-polar AlGaN/GaN high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) on sapphire incorporating an AlGaN back-barrier for W-band operation is demonstrated. The device achieves a subthreshold slope of ~130 mV/dec, a peak transconductance of 0.75 S/mm, and an fmax exceeding 240 GHz. Continuous-wave load-pull measurements at 94 GHz show an output power of 3.75 W/mm with a power-added efficiency of 31.8%. This performance significantly exceeds the best previously reported Ga-polar devices on sapphire and approaches that of state-of-the-art Ga-polar devices on SiC, which provides a promising pathway toward high-performance W-band devices.

items.title: Coherent Optical Control of a Single Donor Electron Spin
items.abstract: Coherent spin-photon interfaces are essential for scalable quantum networks, but their realization requires optically bright transitions, long-lived spin coherence, and complete coherent control. Donor-bound electron spins in II-VI semiconductors offer an attractive platform for optically active spin qubits because they combine strong donor-bound exciton transitions in a direct-bandgap material with a potentially nuclear-spin-free environment. However, coherent control of an individual optically active donor spin has remained elusive. Here we demonstrate optical initialization, coherent control, and readout of a single donor-bound electron spin in ZnSe. Using spin-selective donor-bound exciton optical transitions, we initialize the electron spin and directly resolve its spin-relaxation dynamics. We achieve coherent spin control with off-resonant picosecond optical pulses, as demonstrated...

items.title: High-Efficiency Graphene Oxide Moiré Lenses Enabled by Cyclic Self-Assembly and Laser Nanoprinting
items.abstract: Compact optical systems with continuously tunable focal lengths are highly desirable for machine vision, biomedical imaging, and miniaturized cameras. Rotational Moiré lenses offer a planar approach to focal-length tuning, but metasurface-based implementations typically require complex nanofabrication processes that complicate large-area production. Here, we present a cyclic, mask-free fabrication strategy that combines layer-by-layer self-assembly of two-dimensional graphene oxide (GO) and poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) (PDDA) with femtosecond laser nanoprinting. Repeated GO-PDDA assembly and spatially selective ablation enable atomic-scale thickness control and the construction of precise multilevel phase profiles, reducing phase-quantization errors and improving focusing efficiency. The measured focusing efficiencies of individual GO lenses increase from 22.4% for two phase le...

items.title: Multiwavelength Photoluminescence as a Non-destructive Probe of Depth-Dependent UV Damage in Perovskite Semiconductors
items.abstract: Buried interfaces play a critical role in the operational stability of perovskite optoelectronic devices, yet remain challenging to probe non-destructively. Here, we demonstrate a multiwavelength photoluminescence-based approach exploiting the wavelength-dependent absorption of perovskites, enabling fast, and non-destructive probing of depth-sensitive degradation behavior of perovskite devices under operational conditions. Using ultraviolet (UV) light-soaking with different indium tin oxide (ITO) modifiers as a test case, we employ wide-field photoluminescence (PL) imaging, time-resolved photoluminescence (trPL) and ideality factor measurements with different wavelength excitation to characterize degradation behavior of both perovskite thin films and photovoltaic devices under UV soaking. Using only nondestructive characterization, we show that UV-induced degradation in p-i-n perovskite...

items.title: Generation of quantum light with tunable Wigner negativity with a semiconductor quantum dot
items.abstract: Wigner-negative states of light are key resources for quantum advantage in continuous-variable optical quantum computing. They can be produced probabilistically via frequency conversion and photon detection, or deterministically by exploiting the single-photon nonlinearity of a quantum emitter. Here, we generate such Wigner-negative states of light with a tunable negativity using a single semiconductor quantum dot in a cavity. Optical coherent control of the quantum-dot transition allows to generate a quantum superposition of zero and one photon. The generated quantum states are characterized point-by-point in the phase space through homodyne measurement. The emergence of Wigner-function negativity is observed as the excitation power is increased. After correcting for collection and propagation losses, we obtain fidelities to the ideal state and quantum purities above 95%, together with...

The undergraduate curriculum of electrical and computer engineering and computer science programs has not evolved accordingly. Core courses cover the design and the functionality of hardware while the security aspects remain overlooked, and dedicated hardware security (HS) courses are elective, scarce, and often restricted to graduate students. items.abstract: Multiplexing and photonic-electronic integration offer a route to scalable and high-throughput quantum key distribution (QKD) networks through parallel transmission and compact hardware suited to volume manufacturing. items.abstract: Reliable temperature measurement is essential for characterizing and engineering two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor devices, yet optical thermometry of 2D materials has so far been demonstrated only over narrow temperature windows spanning a few hundred kelvin. Here, we establish a comprehensive optical thermometry framework for monolayer WS2 from 5~K to 1273~K. items.title: A van der Waals Floating-Gate Platform for Broadband Optoelectronic Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: Artificial synapses that integrate nonvolatile memory with broadband optoelectronic learning are essential for next-generation neuromorphic computing. Here, we report a van der Waals ReS2/hBN/InSe floating-gate synaptic transistor that combines efficient charge storage with broadband optoelectronic learning in a single device architecture. The heterostructure incorporates InSe as a floating-gate layer for stable charge storage, hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) as a tunneling dielectric, and ReS2 as a photoresponsive channel, enabling carrier tunneling under electrical and optical stimulation. items.title: Photoinduced charging and spatially selective photochemistry on ferroelectric surfaces
items.abstract: Ferroelectric surfaces exhibit polarization-dependent photoreactivity and provide a route to program chemical patterns through local electrical control of polarization. Observations accumulated over several decades show reaction products in domain interiors, at domain boundaries, and in other selected regions, indicating that the mechanisms extend beyond a single polarization-induced band-bending picture. Here we analyze light-induced charging and interfacial reactions on uniformly polarized ferroelectrics and domain patterns, for dry surfaces and surfaces in contact with an electrochemically active solution. items.title: ChroNoC: A Tableless TDM Circuit-Switched NoC With Delay-Aware Deployment for Time-Sensitive Neuromorphic Computing
items.abstract: Time-sensitive neuromorphic architectures require predictable interconnects to preserve precise event timing. Statically scheduled time-division-multiplexed (TDM) circuit-switched networks-on-chip (NoCs) provide deterministic latency at the cost of linear configuration-memory scaling with schedule depth. Furthermore, jointly optimizing task placement, routing, and scheduling creates an intractable combinatorial search space. Existing deployment frameworks also ignore algorithmic axonal delays by forcing immediate spike injections that increase network contention. This paper proposes a hardware-software co-design to address these challenges. ChroNoC is a tableless TDM NoC that embeds precomputed full-grid broadcast trees into combinational logic as a fixed routing substrate. This fixed substrate reduces deployment to a spatial search via Delay-Aware Reservations and Spatial Annealing (DAR...

items.title: Nonreciprocal magneto-optic beam steering of thermal emission
items.abstract: Conventional thermal emitters obey Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation, which ties absorptivity to emissivity and places a fundamental limit on a range of radiative energy technologies and sensing systems. This constraint can be overcome using magneto-optic materials, which exhibit nonreciprocal thermal emission under an applied magnetic field. While the spectral nonreciprocity of magneto-optic devices has been explored theoretically and experimentally, nonreciprocal control over the direction of thermal emission has received far less attention. Here, we propose and numerically demonstrate nonreciprocal beam steering of thermal emission, wherein an applied magnetic field lifts the degeneracy between guided modes at +/- kx, enabling asymmetric and tunable directional thermal emission. We highlight a III-V semiconductor photonic structure operating at 24.5 um, a wavelength with few laser...

items.title: Surface Functionalization with Lasers: from Nanostructures to Applications
items.abstract: Pulsed laser sources stand out as remarkable and versatile tools in the growing interdisciplinary field of materials science, offering capabilities for tailoring and customizing materials to meet specific requirements. Their ability to induce different controlled material alterations allows enhancing material properties that might otherwise remain elusive. In essence, laser-induced material modifications encompass a spectrum of transformative processes, ranging from subtle topographical changes in the nano- and microscale, to intricate chemical modifications. Among the challenges to overcome are the creation of approaches that allow tuning the properties of light to optimize interactions on various types of solids, including metals, semiconductors, and dielectrics. Understanding these interactions is paramount towards efficiency increase of the processing techniques. This chapter embarks...

items.title: Emergent parafermions with tunable localization in a quantum circuit network
items.abstract: \noindent Quantum circuit simulators with hybrid metal-semiconductor dots provide a versatile platform to realize Kondo anyons. These arise at critical points driven by frustrated Kondo screening of dot charge degrees of freedom and have been demonstrated experimentally in linear circuits of one or two dots. Here we study a triangular triple dot device, where geometric frustration gives rise to an emergent $\mathbb{Z}_3$ parafermion shared among the three dots. We show that the parafermion can be tunably relocated to any pair of dots by applying gate voltages, and is supported in both the weak-tunneling `Kondo limit' and the strong transmission `quasiballistic' regime. The critical states survive strong coupling to external leads and other dots, establishing the basis for a scalable and reconfigurable network architecture in which non-Abelian excitations can be realized and manipulated.

items.title: When Protection Hurts: A Cytokine Storm Theory of Supply Chain Overreaction
items.abstract: Supply chain resilience research has traditionally viewed defensive actions such as safety stock, backup suppliers, expedited transportation, and emergency sourcing as beneficial. However, disruptions such as the COVID-19 pandemic, the 2021 semiconductor shortage, and the Suez Canal blockage highlight how synchronized hoarding, duplicate ordering, and capacity reservation can amplify congestion and operational costs, sometimes worsening the original disruption. Motivated by this observation, we develop a decision-theoretic framework in which Protective Response Intensity (PRI) is an endogenous decision variable. We introduce Response-Induced Loss (RIL) to capture costs generated by defensive actions and characterize a unique optimal response that balances disruption mitigation against self-induced losses. We derive a closed-form critical response threshold beyond which RIL exceeds the or...

items.title: Optical imaging with only the evanescent fields and without diffraction
items.abstract: We report on a conceptual framework for optical imaging utilizing exclusively evanescent fields, effectively eliminating or attenuating standard optical diffraction. We present the theoretical foundation of this concept based on the decomposition of dipole radiation into evanescent fields and homogeneous propagating waves, exploring the explicit conditions required to suppress the latter. By successfully decoupling and removing the homogeneous component, optical tasks, such as sub-diffraction imaging, can be executed solely via evanescent channels, bypassing traditional diffractive limits. We discuss the physical feasibility of this approach and provide concrete examples of how this conjecture can be realized using currently available laboratory and industrial techniques. items.abstract: Electron-phonon interactions govern quasiparticle energies, lifetimes, and temperature-dependent band structures in semiconductors. However, direct momentum-resolved experimental evidence of their impact on quasiparticle electronic structure remains scarce, particularly in nitride semiconductors. Here, we present conclusive experimental evidence of electron-phonon interaction-induced quasiparticle renormalization and pronounced spectral broadening in p-type scandium nitride (ScN), using soft x-ray angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy. items.title: Charge state and hydration of vacancies in silicon and silicon carbide in contact with water: A grand-canonical first-principles stability map
items.abstract: The state of a vacancy in a semiconductor is normally described by the Fermi level alone. In wet-etched, electrochemically processed, or humid silicon and silicon carbide, a vacancy also takes up hydrogen and oxygen from water, in amounts set by pH and electrode potential. We treat both effects together by minimizing the grand potential of a vacancy complex over its charge state and hydrogen/oxygen content. The result is a stability map in Fermi level and hydrogen chemical potential, which the computational hydrogen electrode relates to pH and potential. We parameterize it with spin-polarized density functional theory in 64-atom cells, including the vibrational free energy of bound H and O, for the silicon vacancy, its H, O, and OH complexes, and both vacancies of 3C-SiC. items.title: Physics Informed Neural Networks for Solving the Drift-Diffusion Equations
items.abstract: The drift-diffusion equations are the fundamental building block for the modeling, design, and optimization of modern semiconductor devices. Solutions of the drift-diffusion equations rarely give way to analytical forms, and exhibit strong nonlinearity, with the solutions ranging over several orders of magnitude. These attributes have led to research into numerical solvers, and while many commercial Technology Computer Aided Design (TCAD) packages now exist, they may require long simulation times, exhibit sensitivity to initial guesses, and rely on mesh generation. Further, these solvers are not well suited for inverse problems where the design parameters of a device are retrieved from its desired functional characteristics. To address all these challenges, this work demonstrates the usage of Physics Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) for the solution of the drift-diffusion equations with...

items.title: Automated Multi-Line Bug Repair Using Model Checker Aided LLMs: A Case Study on RISC-V Processors
items.abstract: Functional verification of Register-Transfer Level(RTL) designs has become a critical bottleneck in modern semiconductor development, often consuming the majority of project resources. Debugging, in particular, remains an especially time-consuming task, requiring careful analysis of simulation traces or counterexamples. Recent work has explored applying Large Language Models (LLMs) to RTL debug and repair with great promise. However, the existing approaches typically are for single-line bugs, operate in open-loop, rely heavily on prompts or retrieval, lack scalability, and often produce incorrect fixes. In this paper, we propose a novel automated RTL bug repair methodology that combines LLMs, assertions, and a model checker to provide scalable, trustworthy semantic grounding and formal guarantees. items.title: Sub-monolayer tracking of molecular states at buried interfaces
items.abstract: Phenomena responsible for emerging technologies originate from novel molecular states at buried interfaces. Yet quantitatively resolving these features is out of reach in most cases. Resonant soft X-ray scattering (RSoXS) has demonstrated sensitivity to these local states but is limited due to a lack of accurate interpretive models and spatial resolution. items.title: Localization Contrast As a Fundamental Limit of Radiative Quantum Efficiency
items.abstract: Disorder can localize valence- and conduction-band states to different degrees, yet whether such localization contrast has observable consequences remains poorly understood. Here, we show that localization contrast strongly impacts competing carrier-recombination channels. We illustrate this behavior in random In$_x$Ga$_{1-x}$N alloys. Increasing the In content from $x=13.5\%$ to $x=22\%$ progressively localizes the valence-band maximum state while leaving the conduction-band minimum state comparatively delocalized. This contrasting localization decreases the interband optical momentum matrix element underlying radiative recombination. For Auger-Meitner recombination, however, localization alone does not determine the coupling; atomic-scale disorder also breaks primitive-cell translational symmetry and modifies the momentum-space and phase structure of the states. items.abstract: Ultrafast laser excitation of carriers in semiconductors often results in the creation of fully symmetric coherent optical phonons, typically understood in terms of a thermalized transient carrier population. We test this understanding with systematic measurements and first-principles calculations of the photon-energy dependence of ultrafast-laser-driven coherent phonon generation in tellurium, using excitation wavelengths around the electronic band gap. We observe that, contrary to the expectations of models assuming a thermalized carrier population, the coherent amplitude of the fully symmetric $A_1$ mode changes only weakly when tuning wavelength across the band gap. The measured spectral dependence is instead reproduced by a transition-resolved prethermal force weighted by optical matrix elements and band- and momentum-dependent $A_1$ deformation potentials. items.title: Passive-reflector bounds and robust bilateral nonequilibrium Casimir repulsion
items.abstract: Nonequilibrium electromagnetic fluctuations can generate repulsive Casimir--Lifshitz pressures, but optimizing a cavity at one operating point does not establish that the repulsion survives uncertainty or exceeds ordinary far-field radiation pressure. We formulate a two-sided biased-semiconductor cavity as a constrained max--min problem that maximizes the smaller outward pressure on its two reflectors. In the optically thick-slab limit, identical reflectors admit a symmetric global optimizer, and a passive-reflector bound separates cavity enhancement from the driven far-field plateau. At $300~\mathrm{K}$, a biased-GaAs cavity with $\pm10~\mathrm{nm}$ gap uncertainty and $\pm0.005$ drive uncertainty sustains a worst-case pressure of $2.257~\mathrm{mPa}$ with ideal reflectors. Reoptimization with a causal gold response retains $2.164~\mathrm{mPa}$. The nominal and robust optima lie within...

items.title: Hierarchical Fourier Phase Projection for Local Electronic Observables
items.abstract: We develop hierarchical Fourier phase projection (HPP) to evaluate electronic observables without explicitly constructing occupied eigenstates. Nested Fourier probes progressively cancel nearby cross terms, while exponential or algebraic density-matrix decay suppresses distant contributions. Refinement reuses all previous matrix-function responses to evaluate diverse electronic observables. Electron density and nonlocal forces illustrate diagonal extraction and off-diagonal contraction, respectively. A locality-based decay model fitted to changes across completed levels estimates residual errors from the unresolved pairs without additional matrix-function applications. Tests using fixed Kohn-Sham Hamiltonians for semiconductors, metals, and thermally perturbed silica cover different decay ranges and periodic cell geometries. About 90% of the assessed density and nonlocal force prediction...

items.title: SimSkip: StrongARM-Comparator Similarity Sensing with SAR-Skipping-Aware Training for Analog Compute-in-Memory
items.abstract: Analog-to-digital conversion dominates the energy and area of analog compute-in-memory (CIM) accelerators. This paper presents SimSkip, a successive-approximation-register (SAR) skipping scheme that combines a lightweight StrongARM-comparator similarity detector with SAR-skipping-aware training. When two held voltages are similar, the upper bits of the preceding code are reused to skip SAR comparisons. Detector-induced disturbance extracted from 55-nm CMOS simulations and bit-exact prefix saturation are embedded in the forward pass, and the network learns to tolerate them through quantization-aware training and knowledge distillation. On an ISAAC-based W4A4 WRN-28-10, SimSkip achieves 77.23% CIFAR-100 top-1 accuracy (mean of three seeds) versus 78.4% for the baseline, while reducing SAR comparisons by 48.2% across three hardware-modeled layers. A first-order model estimates a 27.2% net A...

items.title: Laser-Induced Rashba Spin-Orbit Torques in Multiferroic Semiconductor (Ge,Mn)Te
items.abstract: The multiferroic semiconductor (Ge,Mn)Te exhibits ferroelectricity, strong Rashba spin-orbit coupling, and carrier-mediated magnetic order, making it a unique platform for exploring the interplay between electronic, structural, and magnetic degrees of freedom. In this study, we investigate the ultrafast magnetization dynamics of Ge0.85Mn0.15Te using time-resolved magneto-optical spectroscopy. By separating magnetic and nonmagnetic contributions in the transient response, we identify two distinct laser-induced magnetic phenomena, both arising from a photoinduced effective spin-orbit torque. Coherent magnetization precession is driven by a laser-induced increase in hole concentration, which modifies the occupation of Rashba split, spin-locked valence band states and shifts the position of the magnetic easy axis. items.title: A swept-source dual-comb spectrometer on a chip
items.abstract: Dual-comb spectroscopy (DCS) enables high-speed, high-resolution spectroscopy by down-converting optical spectra to the radio-frequency (RF) domain through the interference of two mutually detuned frequency combs. Accurately resolving narrow molecular absorption features requires closely spaced comb lines generated by large laser cavities with long round-trip times, thereby hindering the miniaturization of high-resolution spectrometers. Here, we circumvent this limitation by demonstrating a swept-source dual-comb spectrometer using two unidirectional racetrack semiconductor lasers integrated on the same chip. The traveling-wave frequency combs are generated by strong RF injection at the laser cavity round-trip frequency of 14.3~GHz---otherwise known as quantum walk combs---and are continuously tuned in frequency by varying the laser drive currents. This enables continuous spectral sampli...

items.title: Inverse-Designed High-Q and Small-Mode-Volume Silicon Nitride Photonic Crystal Cavities for Second- and Third-Harmonic Generation
items.abstract: SiN photonic crystal (PhC) cavities are promising platforms for nonlinear and quantum photonics because of their wide transparency window, CMOS compatibility, and negligible two-photon absorption. However, realizing high-Q/V cavities remains challenging because of the relatively low refractive index of SiN. Here, we employ inverse design to optimize a two-dimensional SiN PhC cavity and experimentally demonstrate a quality factor of approximately 80,000, the highest reported for a near-stoichiometric SiN 2D PhC cavity. Furthermore, both second- and third-harmonic generation are observed from the same cavity, providing experimental evidence of strong optical confinement and large Q/V. Our results establish inverse-designed SiN PhC cavities as a promising platform for nonlinear photonics and future heterogeneous integrated photonic devices.

items.title: DACRI: Decision-Aware Causal Intervention Ranking for Critical Supply Chains
items.abstract: Detecting or attributing a supply-chain disruption is not the same as selecting the intervention that maximizes recoverable net value. We present CriticalSCM-Bench v1, a controlled synthetic benchmark with causal ground truth, paired factual/counterfactual rollouts, and an explicit net-value objective. Relative to a full-information train-selected static benchmark, LambdaMART improves median normalized net value by 5.7--16.2\%, with paired statistical support on the semiconductor and critical-material archetypes but not on digital infrastructure. On digital infrastructure, a domain-informed constant-buffer policy remains stronger, showing that greater model complexity is not uniformly justified. Across partial and delayed settings, LambdaMART retains 33--75\% of full-clamp value. Stress tests further show that intervention fidelity, timing, cost, and held-out disruptions can alter policy...

items.title: Real-Time FPGA-Based Multi-Parameter Feedback Stabilization of a Silicon Double Quantum Dot
items.abstract: Long term operation of semiconductor spin qubits requires active stabilization of quantum dot potentials against low-frequency charge noise. To address this, we demonstrate a gradient-descent feedback approach in a silicon double quantum dot device using high-bandwidth radio-frequency (rf) reflectometry readout and a field-programmable gate array (FPGA) for digital signal processing. This architecture enables continuous multi-parameter gradient calculation and quick gate voltage updates, significantly increasing the effective feedback bandwidth compared to previous methods relying on slow direct-current transport measurements. By operating with 8 steps per feedback cycle and an integration time of 25.6 $μ$s, this high-speed stabilization scheme maintains better than -6 dB of noise suppression up to 5 kHz, achieving an attenuation of $-7.4 \pm 0.2$ dB at the maximum measured frequency.
